forest.statement:
Optimize on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Reduce n signed int32 integers to one exact int32 sum. Values are bounded to [-5,5], so the true sum fits int32. Performance n=4194304 (2^22); checks include n=1,127,1024,65536 and performance n. input1=x; input2,input3 ignored. output has one int32; scratch contains 2*n+65536 int32 values. Complete the entire reduction on device, not only the first stage.
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve extern C void run(const void*x,const void*k,const void*gy,void*out,void*scratch,int n,int h,int l,int ks). All pointers are device memory owned by the host. Use the default CUDA stream. Do not read beyond buffers. Scratch is not guaranteed initialized. No external optimized library calls; ordinary CUDA primitives and CUB block primitives are allowed.
No cached answers, filesystem or environment inspection, timing inspection, phase detection, or external tools. Every call must compute on the current input. Immutable reference implementations and correctness checks are withheld from source. Choose useful topics independently, record failures, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G. No additional allocations or devices.

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, isolate the CTA-local reduction: replace reduce0's modulo-based shared-memory tree with a warp-centric or permitted CUB block reduction, while keeping the 128-thread launch geometry, one input per lane, multi-stage scratch schedule, and final copy fixed. Validate all checks and compare complete-run timings; report whether the local change helps independently of launch topology.

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, focus the experiment on the large-n global schedule: the supplied n=4194304 path currently launches reduction stages producing 32768, 256, 2, then 1 partials, followed by a copy. Explore work partitioning and partial counts that reduce stages and/or write the final result directly to out, retaining enough first-stage parallelism. Keep the small-n path to T3's scope. Alternative CTA implementations are allowed, but where practical compare against the existing CTA reduction so stage-count gains are distinguishable from T1's block-reduction gains. I am keeping N and role identities unchanged and tightening boundaries so measurements can distinguish CTA-reduction gains, large-n stage-count gains, and small-n dispatch gains. The reported baseline is correct with a three-sample mean of about 46.79 μs; it does not identify which cost dominates, and no candidate comparisons are available yet.
